report:
Reviewed the complete fresh crates.sage_ir.types.calls.dispatch_families claim and every current association. Requirements: completed calls distinguish direct function definitions, static trait-method dispatch, dynamic trait-object dispatch, function-pointer dispatch, and callable-trait dispatch through each of Fn, FnMut and FnOnce. Receiver/coercion operations must already be explicit expression-tree nodes rather than an adjustment list requiring replay. All families and this representation constraint must be accounted for.

The only implementation association is the explicit sage_meta::todo entry in crates/sage-meta/tests/representation_spec.rs, stating that dynamic, function-pointer and callable-trait dispatch and the complete substitution/adjustment matrix remain pending. The only associated test, sage_meta::todo::types_calls_dispatch_families, contains the same TODO and no assertions. There is no ordinary test or N/A evidence for this anchor, so no behavioral coverage is credited from the placeholder.

Captured the current CallDispatch and ResolvedCallTarget definitions. CallDispatch represents Direct and StaticTrait, the latter carrying Self type and trait reference. ResolvedCallTarget stores a function identity, that dispatch enum, owner type arguments and method type arguments. This is partial representation for the first two families, not the claimed full dispatch family set. There are no dynamic, pointer or callable-family alternatives in this captured dispatch enum. Its lack of an adjustment-list field also does not by itself prove all receiver/coercion operations are materialized correctly in completed trees.

Captured the typed-IR calls/receiver guide and accepted completed-body rationale. They explain explicit receiver nodes and the need for typed-tree fixtures across every family as supported. The guide's current-slice examples and conceptual Clone tree are design context, not execution evidence for this anchor. The existing TODO accurately identifies missing dispatch support and the full adjustment matrix without discarding the current Direct/StaticTrait representation.

Replacing the deferral requires representing and selecting dynamic trait-object, function-pointer and Fn/FnMut/FnOnce dispatch alongside the existing families, plus annotated completed-tree fixtures distinguishing all families and directly inspecting receiver/coercion nodes. Direct and static-trait cases also need evidence within that complete matrix; current enum variants alone are not tests. No replayable adjustment list may remain in successful output. All claim requirements are retained, with no N/A exemption or specification weakening.

Validation was source inspection through review start/read. No source changes or behavioral tests were performed; centrally run suites remain separate execution evidence. No requested edits: the implementation/test TODO honestly records the incomplete family and adjustment coverage, while partial representation is not promoted to a complete verdict.
